nodes.label: Type Safety as a Boundary
nodes.rationale: Configuration parsing, schema validation, dependency checks, and shell lint are treated as compiler boundaries so invalid states cannot be bypassed or silently accepted.

nodes.label: Deployment Adapter Boundary
nodes.rationale: Static deployment is separated from shell runtime ownership so shell availability does not depend on chezmoi or broad copying over active machine state.

nodes.label: Behavior-First Migration
nodes.rationale: Historical management-layer churn showed that behavior, ownership, and configuration contracts should be stabilized before choosing or expanding a deployment engine.

nodes.label: Explicit Migration Rollback
nodes.rationale: Rollback is explicit because automation cannot safely infer which preexisting application file or legacy runtime should be authoritative.

nodes.label: Compiler as Verification Boundary
nodes.rationale: Compiler errors prevent invalid states without relying on intention or additional tests, so type boundaries must not be cast around or overridden.

nodes.label: Validated Red-Green Checkpoints
nodes.rationale: Committing and pushing each validated failing and passing checkpoint preserves executable evidence of behavior changes.

nodes.label: Pull Request Follow-Through
nodes.rationale: Deliverables should be represented by a pull request whose latest head is followed until green so stated completion is backed by remote validation.
